content.text:
I added sign-up and sign-in (email + password, plus Google) using **WorkOS AuthKit**, and `/dashboard` now requires a session. Lint and `next build` both pass. Against a local production server with placeholder credentials, `/` loads, and `/dashboard`, `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` all redirect to the WorkOS sign-in page. I haven't tested a full sign-in, because that needs a real WorkOS account and credentials.

**Why WorkOS:** the sign-in and sign-up forms, password storage, email verification and Google OAuth are all hosted by WorkOS. Your user store is an in-memory array, so a library that keeps passwords itself (Auth.js, Better Auth) would first need a real database and its own password security. The free tier covers up to 1M monthly active users. The trade-off is depending on an outside service, and the forms look like WorkOS's hosted pages unless you restyle them in their dashboard.

**What changed**
- `src/proxy.ts`: Next 16 runs this before every request. Matched paths require a session unless they're on the public list (`/`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/auth/callback`), so `/dashboard` and anything under it is blocked by default.
- `src/app/sign-in/route.ts`, `src/app/sign-up/route.ts`: send the visitor to the hosted WorkOS form, then back to `/dashboard`.
- `src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`: finishes the sign-in and creates or links the Notely user.
- `src/lib/users.ts`:
  - `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session instead of always returning the first user.
  - New `requireCurrentUser()` redirects visitors who aren't signed in; the dashboard uses it as a second guard.
  - New `upsertUserFromAuth()` matches a WorkOS user to a Notely user:
    - First it looks for a saved WorkOS ID (stored in a new optional `authId` field).
    - Otherwise it matches an existing row by email, but only if WorkOS has verified that email, so nobody can sign up as `ada@example.com` and take over her account.
    - If neither matches, it creates a new user.
- **Sign out:** a button on the home page and dashboard.
- **Home page:** the Next.js starter page is replaced with sign-in / create-account buttons, or a welcome message when signed in. The page title is now "Notely".
- **Packages:** added `@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs` and `@workos-inc/node`.
- **`.env.example`:** placeholder credentials. `.gitignore` was ignoring every `.env*` file, so I added `!.env.example` to let this one be committed.

**Before it works for real**
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in your values. Generate the cookie password with `openssl rand -base64 32`.
2. In the WorkOS dashboard:
   - Turn on **Email + Password** and **Google OAuth**. The Google button appears on the hosted form, not in the app code.
   - Add `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as a redirect URI.
   - Set a sign-out URI.

**Worth knowing**
- Users are still kept only in memory, as before, so anyone who signs up disappears when the server restarts. They're recreated automatically the next time they sign in, but they'll get a new ID. Storing them in a database is the next step.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` on its own reports `LayoutProps` as missing in `layout.tsx`. That was already the case before my changes: Next generates that type during build, and the build passes.

Nothing is committed; all the changes are in the working tree.
